NormalizedChapter.description:
A YouTube chapter marker. Grounded, but stage-level — never a node duration.

See design doc §0: a chapter delta measures how long the creator spent on screen,
not how long the cook will spend. Used only by `corroborate.py`.

start_sec.description: Chapter start, in seconds from video start.
start_sec.title: Start Sec

end_sec.description: Chapter end, in seconds. Null for the last chapter if unknown.
end_sec.title: End Sec

NormalizedChapter.title: NormalizedChapter

NormalizedIngredient.description:
One ingredient line, structured but not yet graph-ready.

`qty` stays a free-text string, not a float: real sources state quantities as
"a little less than 2", "1/2", or ranges, which cannot be honestly forced into a
single number here. `graph.py` does that best-effort conversion, not this model.

name.description: As named in the source. Never invented.
name.title: Name

qty.description: Quantity as stated, verbatim or lightly normalized.
qty.title: Qty

prep_note.description: Stated on the ingredient line itself, e.g. "finely chopped".
prep_note.title: Prep Note

group.description: Ingredient grouping, e.g. "For tadka", when the source states one.
group.title: Group

NormalizedIngredient.title: NormalizedIngredient

NormalizedStep.description:
One candidate node, before `graph.py` decides how to build it.

Mirrors the shape of `Node` closely enough that `graph.py` is mostly a direct
translation, but stays looser where real sources are messy (`duration_*` as
`float | None` rather than required ints) and adds the hint/verification fields
§10.C's independent-verification rule needs.

text.description: The step, lightly normalized. Never invented.
text.title: Text

label.description: A short (1-4 word) UI heading for this step -- a summary in your own words (e.g. "Mix marinade", "First rise"), not a truncation of text. Null if you have none. graph.py accepts it only by shape (word count, no leading conditional marker, no trailing preposition/conjunction) and falls back to its own trim of `text` otherwise -- it is never checked against `text` for topical match, so accuracy is still your job.
label.title: Label

attention.description: The model's classification. MUST default to hands_on when no explicit cue is present (design doc §5) — graph.py re-checks this via attention_cue before trusting periodic/unattended.
attention.title: Attention

attention_cue.description: Verbatim source phrase justifying periodic/unattended. Null when attention is hands_on. graph.py must confirm this string actually appears in the source text before honoring a non-hands_on attention.
attention_cue.title: Attention Cue

duration_stated.description: True only if a number was written in the source text; False if this is a plausible estimate from a vague-but-present cue ("cook until golden"). graph.py applies the §4.7 low-end clamp (duration_typical = duration_min) to window-host nodes when this is False.
duration_stated.title: Duration Stated

depends_on_previous.description: LEGACY (prompt v1/v2). Consecutive stated steps default to sequential (§4.7). False only when the model asserts genuine independence; graph.py still applies the two-condition test (no shared ingredient/component, no produces/consumes link) before honoring False. Ignored once depends_on_steps is provided.
depends_on_previous.title: Depends On Previous

depends_on_steps.description: 0-based positions of the EARLIER steps whose output or pan/vessel state this step directly needs. [] means it genuinely needs nothing earlier. None means not provided -- graph.py then falls back to depends_on_previous. A claim, not a fact: graph.py verifies it.
depends_on_steps.title: Depends On Steps

role.description: required: part of cooking the dish. optional: conditional or nice-to-have ("If you plan to...", "if desired"). alternative: another way to do an earlier step ("Microwave method: ..."). Never drop an optional/alternative instruction; mark it here instead.
role.title: Role

role_cue.description: Verbatim source phrase showing the step is optional/alternative. Null when role is required. graph.py must find it in the source text before honoring a non-required role.
role_cue.title: Role Cue

attach_to_step.description: 0-based position of the required step this optional/alternative instruction belongs with. Null when role is required.
attach_to_step.title: Attach To Step

consumes_ingredients.description: Ingredient names (matching NormalizedIngredient.name), OR a produces_component label from an earlier step, when this step uses that earlier step's output.
consumes_ingredients.title: Consumes Ingredients

produces_component.description: Freeform label for what this step yields -- set it only when a LATER step will name this exact label in its own consumes_ingredients.
produces_component.title: Produces Component

station.description: Explicit if stated; else the §4.7 verb-based default.
station.title: Station

interruptible.description: Almost never stated; §4.7 default is prep=true, active/finish=false.
interruptible.title: Interruptible

freshness.description: See module docstring: never invent a number for stated_unbounded.
freshness.title: Freshness

freshness_cue.description: Verbatim source phrase, when freshness != none. graph.py should require this to carry a genuine immediacy marker ("immediately", "just before serving") before trusting stated_unbounded — a bare "serve" is not one (§10.C finding 3).
freshness_cue.title: Freshness Cue

max_lead_min.description: ONLY populated for stated_numeric. Never a guessed number.
max_lead_min.title: Max Lead Min

doneness_cue.description: A qualitative phrase, only if textually present, e.g. "until golden".
doneness_cue.title: Doneness Cue

NormalizedStep.title: NormalizedStep

description:
The real, inspectable value that crosses the normalize -> graph seam.

`method_grounded` is the model's own claim and MUST NOT be trusted as-is
(§10.C finding 1): `normalize.py`'s Tier 0 gate recomputes it as `bool(steps)`
before any caller acts on it.

title.description: A clean dish name (e.g. "Buttermilk Pancakes"), NOT the raw source title verbatim -- the source's own title is preserved separately as ImportResult.source_title regardless of what you put here. Never invent a name unrelated to the source: title.py only accepts this claim when every word in it is grounded in the raw title or a linked blog's own name (case-folded, light stemming), and replaces it with a deterministic cleanup of the raw title otherwise -- so an invented word is simply discarded, not shown to the cook.
title.title: Title

method_grounded.description: The model's own claim about whether method text existed. A hint only — callers must independently verify via `bool(steps)`.
method_grounded.title: Method Grounded

servings.description: How many PEOPLE this feeds — only if the source states that, in those terms. Never the yield count (how many pieces/items the recipe makes) — that goes in yield_text instead. If the source only gives a piece count ("makes 14 rasgulla") with no separate people count, leave this null; do not copy the piece count here.
servings.title: Servings

yield_text.description: The source's own stated yield, verbatim or lightly trimmed — whatever it actually says it makes ("14 rasgulla", "2 loaves", "8 people"), including a unit/item word even when that's just a count of people. Only if a number is stated; null if the source gives no number at all ("makes a dozen" has no digit — leave this null rather than converting words to a number).
yield_text.title: Yield Text

stated_total_min.description: ONLY an explicit stated total-time claim. Never derived from video duration.
stated_total_min.title: Stated Total Min

notes.description: Free-text notes for a human reviewer: ambiguities, translation doubts, etc.
notes.title: Notes
